There will be someone who will demonstrate one day in which parts the Comets wander. Since they go so removed from the others, how great and what kind they are. We are content with what has been discovered, may posterity contribute something to the truth. Through the stars, he says, we do not discern what is beyond, but through Comets we transmit our gaze. First, if that happens, it does not happen in that part where the star itself is of dense and solid fire, but where a rare splendor runs out and scatters into hair. You see through the intervals of the fires, not through them themselves. All stars, he says, are round; Comets are elongated, from which it appears they are not stars. But who will grant you that Comets are long, when their nature is indeed like the others, a globe? Moreover, the brightness is extended just as the sun sends its rays far and wide. But the form of the body itself is one thing, and the light that flows from it is another. Thus, the body of the Comets itself is rounded. The splendor, however, appears longer than that of the other stars. Why, you ask? Tell me first why the moon receives light so very different from the sun, when it receives it from the sun? Why does it now redden, now grow pale? Why is its color livid and black when it is excluded from the sight of the sun? Tell me why all stars have a face in some way unlike each other, and most diverse from the sun. How does nothing prevent the stars from being what they are, even if they are not similar, just as nothing prevents Comets from being eternal and of the same lot as the others, even if they do not have a similar face? Furthermore, if you consider the world itself, is it not composed of diverse things? Why is it that the sun always burns in the lion <note>the zodiac sign Leo</note>, and scorches the lands with heat? In the water-bearer <note>the zodiac sign Aquarius</note>, it constricts winter and closes rivers with frost? And yet this star and that one are of the same condition <margin>† arises</margin>, although they are dissimilar in effect and nature. Within a very short time, the ram <note>the zodiac sign Aries</note> † rises, the scales <note>the zodiac sign Libra</note> set most slowly, and yet this star and that are of the same nature, although one ascends in a brief time and the other is brought forth for a long while. Do you not see how contrary the elements are to one another? They are heavy and light, cold and hot, moist and dry. The entire concord of this world consists of discord. You deny that a comet is a star because its form does not correspond to the model, nor is it similar to the others. For you see, that one is very similar which returns to its place in the thirtieth year to this one which revisits its seat within a year. Nature does not provide its work according to one form, but prides itself on variety itself. It has made some things more sluggish, others swifter than the rest. It has made some things stronger, others more temperate, but some it has led out from the crowd so that they might proceed individually and conspicuously, and some it has sent into the flock. He who does not think it is allowed for nature to do anything except what it does more frequently is ignorant of its power. It does not show Comets frequently; it attributes to them another place, other times, motions unlike the others. It wished to cultivate the magnitude of its work from these, whose face is too beautiful for you to think them accidental, whether you consider their size or their brightness, which is greater and more fiery than the rest. Its face indeed has something distinguished and singular, not cast into a narrow space and constricted, but released more freely, and embracing the region of many stars. Aristotle says that Comets signify a storm and intemperance of winds and rains. What then? Do you not judge it to be a star because it denounces future events? For it is not a sign of a storm in the way that oil sparkling and rotting fungi growing together are signs of future rain, or how it is an indication of a raging sea if marine coots play on dry land and desert the known marshes, and the heron flies above the high cloud. But it is so, just as the equinox is a sign of the heat and cold of the turning year. Just as those things which the Chaldeans sing of, what a star constitutes for those being born, whether sad or happy. So that you may know this is so, a risen Comet does not immediately threaten winds and rains, as Aristotle says, but <margin>A risen comet makes the whole year suspect.</margin> it makes the whole year suspect. From which it appears that it did not draw the signs it gives for the near future from the immediate proximity, but has them stored and compressed by the laws of the world. That Comet which appeared when Patruculus and Vopiscus were consuls did the things which were predicted by Aristotle and Theophrastus. For there were greatest and continuous storms everywhere. But in Achaia and Macedonia, cities were destroyed by earthquakes. Their slowness, he says, is an argument that they are heavier, and have much of the earthly in them. Their courses, furthermore, are almost driven into the cardinal points. Both are false. I will speak about the former first, that things which are carried more slowly are heavy. What then? <summary>Seneca defends the celestial nature of comets, arguing that variety in the heavens does not negate their status as stars and that their appearance is governed by deep, lawful cycles rather than mere atmospheric disturbances.</summary>
